intelligence.enrichment: Because the Moon moves ahead in its orbit while Earth rotates, it returns to nearly the same sky position about 50 minutes later on the next day. Moon advances in orbit during Earth's daily rotation -> the same sky position is reached later -> moonrise time and sky position shift day by day. The learner correctly applies this rule: Because the Moon moves ahead in its orbit while Earth rotates, it returns to nearly the same sky position about 50 minutes later on the next day. The Moon follows the same daily schedule as the Sun and rises at sunset each day.

spec.instruction: Write one new grades 8 Science question. Chapter: The night sky: Moon and calendars. The student must decide: Predict that the Moon's time and place in the sky change from one day to the next, so it does not always rise when the Sun sets. Use an Indian school or home setting and Indian names. Keep the source language register. Retarget the source onto this Science decision. Keep the source item type. Recalculate the key.
